events.text: Operator stop of the first baseline_ctrl launch (23:33-23:36): its 4 DataLoader workers grew ~1.7 GB private per 30 s each and the machine reached 98.6 % RAM; the OS killed a worker at 23:33:32 (event above). Reproduced in isolation: training-config loader, 1 worker, +1.25 GB per 10 batches (one batch retained per batch); dataset alone in one process: flat. Fix: src/pipeline/stacked_dataset.py::aerotrack_collate stacks into shared memory inside workers (bit-exact vs the old stack; 4 workers flat at ~1.7 GB over 60 batches). A loader-memory probe was added to the pre-flight; the grid was relaunched with the same command at 23:44 and baseline_ctrl restarted from scratch (no epoch had finished).

The pre-flight at 23:24:46 (ok: False) failed only its 'no other GPU job' check: on Windows the venv python.exe is a launcher whose child is the real interpreter, and the check flagged the runner's own launcher (its parent) as a foreign job. Fixed in run_grid.py (ancestors count as the runner's own tree) before any training; the next pre-flight passed every check.

The runner started at 23:44:35 (pid 16996) was killed externally between 01:50:50 and 01:51:52 (no traceback, no event; its console log simply stops). Its training child kept running and finished baseline_ctrl cleanly at 01:53:32 (20/20 epochs, rc 0, recorded by train_ablation.py). Most likely the agent tool that launched the runner cleaned up the process it had started. Mitigations: --detach now starts the runner through a short-lived spawner (never a process of the calling shell), and a relaunched runner first waits for any still-running step of an earlier runner (orphan adoption). Relaunched with the same command; baseline_ctrl is verified from its files, not retrained.

changes: `src/model/preflight.py` — T6 required a 36-channel first convolution (the SPD stem). The stride-2 stem of the `no_spd` and `stock_yolo11n` layouts has 9, so both runs would have aborted before epoch 0. T6 now takes the expected width from the live model (and still requires 9 or 36, so a reload that fell back to 3 channels still fails).

`src/pipeline/stacked_dataset.py::aerotrack_collate` — inside a DataLoader worker the batch is now stacked straight into shared memory, as torch's own `default_collate` does. On this machine the old stack-then-share path left every batch behind in the worker (+118 MB per batch per worker, measured); the first launch of `baseline_ctrl` ran the machine out of memory 3.5 min in and lost a worker. Verified bit-exact against the old stack, flat memory at 4 workers; a loader-memory probe now guards it in the pre-flight.
`src/model/aerotrack_trainer.py` — checkpoints are written to a temporary file and renamed atomically, so an interruption can never leave a truncated `last.pt` (the resume point).
`src/model/train.py` — `--preflight-only`: build the exact job and run T1–T8, train nothing (used to check all four jobs up front).

`scripts/train_ablation.py` — a resumed run keeps ONE `run_meta.json` (first start time, one `attempts` entry per launch, summed training time, workers used) and refuses a changed recipe; `--resume-from`; `--preflight-only`.

`scripts/evaluate_detector.py` — runs trained with temporal_gap 0 (`single_frame`, `stock_yolo11n`) are scored on t,t,t, the input they were trained and validated on (`src/model/train.py::build`), instead of the 3-frame stack; the image set and its hash are unchanged and each row records its `input`. The summary is written after every checkpoint and before the test-ledger line; `--smoke`.

`scripts/render_report.py`, `README.template.md` — grid runs in the run-facts table, an `input` column, verdicts only from finished, hash-matched runs at one budget (rule and target metrics unchanged), plan items 2–4 computed from the grid, a test-ledger note, the one-command reproduction, and a corrected sentence on which COCO tensors are transferred.
new `scripts/run_grid.py` (the one command: pre-flight, sequential training with resume/watchdog, evaluations, test once, reports) and `scripts/grid_report.py` (this report).
Not changed: metrics, splits, image sets, caps, thresholds, the training recipe, the epoch budget, the checkpoint-selection rule, the attribution rule, the COCO-transfer rule.
